To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of students do not believe people with mental disorder are dangerous, but (2) a significant minority do, (3) the majority of respondents do not believe people are blameworthy for mental disorder, but (4) a significant minority disagree, (5) a minority of respondents are unwilling to work on a project with a person with mental disorder.

(1) the majority of students in our sample did not believe that PMD were violent, blameworthy, or that they should be kept off campus; however (2) science students were significantly more negative than arts students, international students were more negative than EU students, and postgraduate students were more negative in several areas than undergraduates; (3) students were more willing than not to work on a project with PMD, but postgraduate and international students were less willing than undergraduates
In summary, our research is concerned with
the attitudes of university students to people with mental disorders.
the attitudes of students towards people with mental disorder and the factors that may influence those attitudes.
mental disorder stigma among university students.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many negative attitudes towards PMD among university students in Scotland.
the attitudes towards people with mental disorder are not as negative as they have been reported to be, and there are some positive attitudes.
there are no significant differences between students of different disciplines, EU students and international students in their attitudes toward mental illness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are many negative attitudes among university students in Scotland towards PMD.
the majority of university students have positive attitudes towards people with mental disorder but a small minority have negative views.
the stigma of mental disorder is still prevalent in Scotland, with the most vulnerable being those who are international students, science students, postgraduate students.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students’ attitudes to PMD are not necessarily as negative as has previously been assumed.
there is a clear need for mental health education for students.
mental illness stigma is still prevalent and that students of different nationalities have different attitudes toward mental illness.
